_comment: Tower Crane per-machine config. COMMITTED template — copy to config.local.json (gitignored)
and fill with this machine's real values. See design\portability.md and README.md.
All fields are non-secret setup pointers — NEVER put tokens or logins here (git/gh auth stays
in its ambient stores: `gh auth login`, `git config`). Keys beginning with _ are ignored by readers.
shared_root: leave this as an empty string. It fills itself in automatically the first time
any tower_crane script runs, computed from wherever this folder actually is — no path to pick,
no convention to follow, works from any location/name. It also self-corrects if the folder is
later moved or renamed (config_lib.py notices the mismatch and tells you to run relocate.py so
already-registered consumers catch up). The one requirement: this repo must live somewhere
under your home directory, since Claude Code's @import only resolves home-relative '~/...' paths.
python_launcher: the command that runs Python 3 on THIS machine. 'python' on Windows;
on macOS/Linux it is usually 'python3' (bare 'python' is often Python 2 or absent) - set it to
whatever `<launcher> --version` reports as Python 3.x here.
publish.* is only needed if you run scripts\publish_release.py (cutting a Replicate release
to a separate public storefront repo). Leave the placeholders if you don't use it.
automation.* (design\sync_automation.md, Piece 3): the unattended ticket-processing agent.
Off by default - flip 'enabled' to true only after running templates\setup_automation.md's
setup, which wires an hourly OS-scheduled task invoking scripts\run_automation.py. 'mode'
has exactly one value for v1 ('propose_only') - reserved for a future narrower auto-apply
tier, not implemented. 'target_remote' only needs a value if this machine's automation should
watch a DIFFERENT hub than this clone's own git remote (rare) - leave empty to default to
identity.git_remote above.
host_id: <this machine's hostname, e.g. the value of %COMPUTERNAME%>

identity.git_remote: <the Tower Crane GitHub remote this clone points at, e.g. https://github.com/you/tower-crane>

publish.public_repo_path: <ABSOLUTE PATH to a persistent local clone of the public storefront repo, e.g. C:\Users\you\Documents\Claude\tower_crane_public>
publish.public_repo_remote: <the public storefront repo's GitHub URL, e.g. https://github.com/you/tower-crane.git>
